nodes.note: Contradicts the theoretical prediction (expected: NMAE worse, FICR better). Measured: BOTH point accuracy (raw_point -0.011491) and FICR (-0.024417) got worse. Zero-gradient region inside the band likely starves the teacher of signal for the majority of well-predicted rows, degrading pc_hat itself and everything downstream (calibration + decision samples).

nodes.name: O3 zero-free-parameter check: is the metric-derived gamma*=1.0 decision point close to the empirical (T,G)-tuned optimum?
nodes.derivation: Total's per-row objective decomposes to argmax[-err(a) + fi(a)] with NO free trade-off weight once fi is normalised by 4*mean_gen (which harness.py already does) -- i.e. gamma*=1.0 is metric-exact, not tuned. This is exactly the T1.0_G1.0 grid point harness.py already scores on every run.
nodes.note: The metric-derived zero-parameter point is close to optimal (within 0.0008-0.0012 of the empirical corner-max in both runs) -- the theoretical claim is largely validated; the residual empirical-tuning gain is small but nonzero and consistently favors G=2.0 (grid corner), echoing the earlier M276 DECISION_TEMPERATURE_IS_CALIBRATION finding. Separately notable: T=1.0 (mildest density-weighting, least sharpened) wins in both runs even after the DEF-1 fix made T non-inert -- sharpening (T<1) does not help within the tested grid.

D_NOG2 solo=0.626160 (tiny +0.000491 over D_REPRO's 0.625669, confirming the harness-level direction), but DEPAVG+D_NOG2=0.631367 vs DEPAVG+D_REPRO(=current_best)=0.636184 -- a LARGE blend regression (-0.004817). G2 apparently contributes ensemble DIVERSITY against DEPAVG that outweighs its tiny solo accuracy cost. CONCLUSION: G2 stays; the earlier 'drop G2' lead is RETRACTED -- it was measured on solo/isolated accuracy without checking blend value, and blend value is what actually matters for current_best. Do not act on solo-accuracy deltas as a proxy for blend value without checking both, per this project's own repeated finding that member diversity and member accuracy are different axes.

nodes.s5_reconstruction_attempt: research/nodes/s9_n8_s5_plus_rews.py: reconstructed S5's teacher_weight/calib_rows/soft_cap from constants surviving in s7_savemembers.py and s10_final3.py, ran S5_only/S5_G2/S5_REWS/S5_G2_REWS through the full protocol. ALL 4 underperformed current_best (-0.0045 to -0.0056), but S5_only's own solo score (0.609699) also falls far short of the real D member's solo score (0.625651) -- the reconstruction is KNOWN-INCOMPLETE, not a real measurement of REWS/G2 value on the true stack. nodes.residual_correction_attempt: research/nodes/s9_n9_rews_residual_correction.py: sidestepped the reconstruction problem entirely by reproducing D's ACTUAL saved prediction (ported s10_final3.py's member() function verbatim from the saved S7-N8_D_keys/prob files) instead of re-deriving it. Reproduction verified essentially exact: solo 0.625669 vs recorded 0.625651, DEPAVG+D(reproduced)=0.636184 matches current_best to 6 decimals -- this reconstruction methodology IS sound. Then fit a per-fold LightGBM L2 regressor on REWS -> (actual - D_prediction) residual, fold-outside. Result: CLEAR NEGATIVE (solo -0.054776, DEPAVG blend -0.004059 vs current_best). Identified cause, not just 'REWS fails': D's prediction is a settlement-optimal ACTION under a step reward, not a conditional mean (this project's standing finding) -- plain L2 residual correction is the wrong objective for that target, so the collapse is consistent with fitting noise rather than REWS lacking information. Closes the plain-L2-residual-correction approach; does not resolve REWS's true value on the real stack.

FIRST RUN HAD A BUG (calling official_total on single-group subsets silently NaN-corrupted the 3-group average -- caught because the n_regimes=1 sanity check returned 0.618830 instead of D's true ~0.6257); the originally-reported -0.001171 delta was WRONG and is retracted. CORRECTED result: DEPAVG+D_REGIME(2 or 3) = 0.635652, delta -0.000532 vs current_best -- closest of any attempt, but both the group-split step and the REWS-regime step are individually slightly negative in isolation, so this is a NULL result for REWS, not 'nearly there' -- the number improved only because the bug stopped corrupting it, not because REWS started helping. This attack line is reasonably exhausted; see registry.json for full detail.
nodes.dart_reconstruction_attempt: research/nodes/s9_n11_dart_s5_rews.py: guessed DART applies to the regression teacher -- WRONG HALF of the pipeline (see true_reconstruction below). Result solo=0.602158/0.605075, worse than several non-DART attempts. Superseded.
nodes.true_reconstruction_and_final_verdict: research/nodes/s9_n12_true_d_plus_rews.py: FOUND THE ACTUAL D-GENERATING SCRIPT via mtime correlation -- research/nodes/s7_more.py (docstring: 'more diverse members: DART boosting, ExtraTrees, a second MLP', MEMS=['D','X','M2']), not s7_savemembers.py (which every prior attempt modeled itself on and only builds P/L/G/Q -- a red herring for D). TRUE architecture: plain GBDT regressor -> pc_hat -> top-150 features by importance + pc_hat + group one-hot -> cf discretized into 26 classes -> a DART-boosted MULTICLASS CLASSIFIER (not a regressor+quantile-table like harness.py, which every S9-N7..N11 attempt wrongly assumed) -> predict_proba -> s10_final3.py's (T,G) policy grid. Exact reproduction verified: D_REPRO solo=0.625669 (matches recorded value exactly), DEPAVG+D_REPRO=0.636184 (matches current_best to 6 decimals) -- fully validated baseline. Added REWS to this TRUE architecture: solo -0.001904, DEPAVG blend -0.003271 vs current_best. DEFINITIVE NEGATIVE -- on the correct, verified architecture, REWS makes things worse, not better. Across all 8 integration attempts this session, none beat current_best; this final one is authoritative. REWS's isolated screening/fold-outside gain (S9-N6, measured against a much weaker unaugmented baseline) does not transfer to the real best model -- it's redundant with or conflicts with what the DART classifier already extracts. Close this line of work; do not pursue REWS further as a path to 0.66.

defects_found.stage: S7 (also present identically in v3.py, a separate S9-adjacent candidate pipeline)
defects_found.desc: Decision layer applied temperature to a UNIFORM sample-INDEX weight vector (np.full(n,1/n)**(1/temp)), which is mathematically invariant to temp after renormalisation -- sharpening was a complete no-op for every node ever scored through harness.py, including current_best.
defects_found.fixed_2026-08-07T12:4x_KST: Added sharpen_weights(samples, temp, n_bins) to research/scratch/lib.py -- bins each row's OWN predictive sample values, weights by bin density, applies temp to that density before renormalising per row. Applied identically in research/scratch/v3.py::act() and research/nodes/harness.py::run(). Verified: (a) unit test confirms different temps now give different weighted means, (b) py_compile clean, (c) two full harness runs (S9-N0, S9-N1) post-fix both completed and produced a real, non-degenerate T-sweep (see S9 nodes above).
defects_found.scope: DEF-1 is confined to harness.py's/v3.py's SAMPLE-based decision layer. current_best (S10-FINAL3, 0.636184) uses a separate, independently-written and verified-correct temperature-scaling path (s10_final3.py) and is not affected -- see S10 caveat_checked_and_cleared. What remains genuinely unresolved: any node scored through harness.py's run()/act() before 2026-08-07T12:4x KST (this session's fix) should not be reused for a temperature-sensitive comparison without re-running.
